feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is claimed for it. Iteration 0 (baseline, y=0.05) is the only design that finishes the oval, at 20/20 in 1.65 s with oscillation 0.15. Its bends failed at progress 0.17 (s-bend) and 0.12 (slalom), with max_error about 0.061 m at the 0.06 m limit. Iteration 3 (y=0.07) collapsed the oval to 0/20 off-track and barely moved the bends (0.21, 0.12), so forward lead is harmful. Iterations 1 and 2 (wide array with 0.5 kg mass) lost oval finishes too, and the mass effect was never isolated from the array. I kept the baseline controller so that only the lead changes. Interpret the next race as follows. If the oval finishes at 20/20 and steering oscillation is at or below 0.15, lead is not the problem, and the bend failure is likely footprint or coverage. If the oval finishes but bends still end at max_error near 0.06 with line loss, change sensor_size to 0.016 at the same y=0.03 layout. If the oval drops below baseline, shorter lead is also wrong, so return to y=0.05 and test spread instead.
requested_changes: If the oval holds at 20/20 at y=0.03 but the s-bend or slalom still end off-track with line_loss_events of 1 or more and max_error near 0.06 m, change sensor_size from 0.012 to 0.016 while keeping y=0.03. Iteration 0 showed max_error 0.061 on both bends at y=0.05, and no run has yet tested footprint size.

If bend progress rises clearly above 0.17 and 0.12 while the oval stays at 20/20, widen x to plus or minus 0.032 m at 16 mm pitch and keep mass at 0.6 kg. Iteration 1 gave a partial bend gain from the wider array (s-bend 0.24, slalom 0.19), but the oval loss in iterations 1 and 2 was confounded with the 0.5 kg mass.

If the oval falls below 20/20 at y=0.03 (for example 18/20 or fewer, with oscillation above 0.15), return the sensor row to y=0.05, the baseline that finished 20/20 in iteration 0. Iteration 3 showed that moving the row away from y=0.05 in either direction costs oval finishes, so the baseline lead may be near the optimum.
